### OVERVIEW  
The Ministry of Education announced that the Supreme Court of India mandated the Teacher Eligibility Test (TET) as a minimum qualification for teachers in schools under the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009, and extended the deadline for compliance to August 31, 2028, while recommending biennial TETconducted twice annually.

### KEY HIGHLIGHTS  
- **Supreme Court Judgment (September 1, 2025):** Declared TET mandatory for teacher appointments in RTE-covered schools under Section 23 of the RTE Act, 2009.  
- **Review Judgment (May 29, 2026):** Extended the TET compliance deadline from August 31, 2027, to August 31, 2028, for pre-2013 appointees.  
- **Periodic TET Conduct:** Directed State Governments and Union Territory Administrations to conduct TET **twice yearly** with approximately six months between exams to facilitate timely compliance.  
- **Constitutional Context:** Education falls under the Concurrent List; teacher recruitment and conditions are administered by State Governments and Union Territory Administrations.

Vice Admiral Manish Chadha, AVSM, VSM, assumed charge as the Director General Naval Operations on 03 Aug 26.

An alumnus of the 78th course of the National Defence Academy, Khadakwasla, Vice Admiral Manish Chadha was commissioned into the Indian Navy on 01 Jul 1991. The Flag Officer is a Communication and Electronic Warfare Specialist. He is an alumnus of the 61st Defence Services Staff College, Wellington, and completed the Higher Command Course at the National Defence University, Washington, USA.

In a distinguished career spanning over 35 years, the Flag Officer has held a wide range of command, operational, instructional, and staff appointments, both afloat and ashore. His key afloat appointments include command of Coast Guard Interceptor Boat CGS-05 and Indian Naval Ships Veer, Kirpan, and Mysore.

The Flag Officer also served as the Naval Attaché at the Embassy of India, Moscow. At Naval Headquarters, he steered several key projects, including projects for VLF and satellite communications, besides serving as the Director, International Fleet Review 2016.

On promotion to Flag Rank, he tenanted the appointments of Flag Officer Commanding Gujarat Naval Area, Assistant Chief of Personnel (Administration and Civilian), Flag Officer Commanding Maharashtra Naval Area, and Assistant Chief of Personnel (Human Resource Development).

On elevation to the rank of Vice Admiral, he was appointed as the Commandant, Indian Naval Academy, where he was responsible for ‘Shaping Future Naval Leadership...’.

In recognition of his distinguished service, the Flag Officer was awarded the Ati Vishisht Seva Medal in 2025 and the Vishisht Seva Medal in 2017.

headline: Government Strengthens Drug De-addiction and Awareness Initiatives in Jammu & Kashmir Under Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan
fullText:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment

Government Strengthens Drug De-addiction and Awareness Initiatives in Jammu & Kashmir Under Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan

Over 1.20 Crore People Sensitised in Jammu & Kashmir; 8,565 Nasha Mukti Mitras Join the Campaign

03 AUG 2026 6:51PM by PIB Delhi

The Central Government is implementing the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan (NMBA) to prevent substance abuse through sustained awareness campaigns, de-addiction, rehabilitation and counselling services across the country. In the Union Territory of Jammu & Kashmir, the campaign has reached more than 1.20 crore people, including over 69.14 lakh youth and 51.20 lakh women, while 8,565 Nasha Mukti Mitras have joined the nationwide movement against drug abuse, as on July 29 this year. The Department of Social Justice and Empowerment is implementing the campaign under the National Action Plan for Drug Demand Reduction (NAPDDR).

Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment Shri B. L. Verma shared the details in a written reply to Shri Aga Syed Ruhullah Mehdi in Lok Sabha. The House was informed that the Ministry provides financial assistance to State Governments, Union Territory Administrations, NGOs and Government Hospitals for preventive education, awareness generation, treatment, rehabilitation and capacity-building programmes to reduce drug demand across the country.

The written reply further stated that the Ministry is supporting a comprehensive network of de-addiction and rehabilitation facilities in Jammu & Kashmir, including Integrated Rehabilitation Centre for Addicts (IRCA), 3 Outreach and Drop-In Centres (ODICs), 2 Community-Based Peer-Led Intervention (CPLI) programmes, 6 District De-Addiction Centres (DDACs), and 21 Addiction Treatment Facilities (ATFs) established in Government hospitals across the Union Territory.

The House was also informed that the Ministry operates the National Toll-Free De-addiction Helpline 14446, which provides primary counselling and referral services. The helpline has received more than 4.6 lakh calls across the country, including over 11,000 calls from Jammu & Kashmir, reflecting increased awareness and accessibility of support services.

The reply further highlighted that the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan, launched on 15 August 2020, has now been expanded to all districts of the country. The campaign focuses on educational institutions, universities and schools to create awareness against substance abuse through community participation. Nationally, the campaign has sensitised more than 29.05 crore people, including over 11.05 crore youth and 7.81 crore women, while more than 1.17 lakh Nasha Mukti Mitras have joined the movement.

Replying to the query regarding assessment of the campaign, the House was informed that the implementation of NMBA is regularly reviewed through monthly review meetings, Chintan Shivirs and National-Level Conferences with States and Union Territories. States and UTs are encouraged to establish and regularly convene State, District and Block-level NMBA Committees to strengthen coordination and ensure effective implementation. These efforts have contributed to sustained awareness generation, increased community participation, stronger inter-departmental coordination, and improved outreach for prevention, treatment and rehabilitation services for persons affected by substance abuse.

47,328 Villages Selected Under PM-AJAY Adarsh Gram Component Across the Country; 435 Villages in Telangana

Over 3.28 Lakh Development Works Identified and More Than 47.59 Lakh Beneficiaries Saturated Under the Scheme

03 AUG 2026 6:45PM by PIB Delhi

The Central Government is implementing the Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana (PM-AJAY) to promote the socio-economic development of Scheduled Caste communities through the integrated development of villages under its Adarsh Gram Component. The scheme aims to ensure saturation of key socio-economic indicators through convergence of Central and State Government schemes while addressing critical development gaps.

Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment Shri Ramdas Athawale, in a written reply to Shri Anil Kumar Yadav Mandadi in the Rajya Sabha, informed that 47,328 villages have been selected across the country under the Adarsh Gram Component of PM-AJAY, including 435 villages in Telangana. State-wise details of the selected villages have been placed on the Table of the House.

The Minister further informed that the Adarsh Gram Component focuses on the integrated development of selected villages through the saturation of 50 monitorable socio-economic indicators across 10 development sectors, including education. A Need Assessment Survey is conducted to establish the baseline status of these indicators. The identified gaps are addressed through convergence with Central and State Government schemes or through interventions supported under PM-AJAY. Progress made by States and Union Territories is regularly updated through the PMAGY Portal.

The House was also informed that, across the country, 3,28,131 development works and 1,10,51,213 beneficiaries have been identified under the scheme. Of these, 46,642 development works have been completed, while 47,59,399 beneficiaries have already been saturated through various interventions.

With regard to Telangana, the written reply stated that under the education sector, 3,529 beneficiaries have been identified, of whom 472 beneficiaries have already received benefits under the scheme.

Replying to a query regarding third-party audit, Shri Athawale informed that States and Union Territories have been directed to verify the self-declaration of Adarsh Gram villages under the PM-AJAY Adarsh Gram Component. Accordingly, validation is being undertaken by the respective State and UT Governments.

The PM-AJAY Adarsh Gram Component continues to promote inclusive and sustainable rural development by improving access to education, infrastructure, livelihoods and essential services, thereby contributing to the socio-economic empowerment of Scheduled Caste communities across the country.

headline: TRAI Assesses Mobile Network Quality Across Haridwar and Rishikesh City under UPW LSA

TRAI Assesses Mobile Network Quality Across Haridwar and Rishikesh City under UPW LSA

03 AUG 2026 6:43PM by PIB Delhi

The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) has released findings of Independent Drive Test (IDT) conducted through its appointed agency across Haridwar and Rishikesh City under UPW LSA, during the month of July 2026, for information of general telecom consumers. The purpose of this drive test is to assess and verify real time quality of mobile network services (both voice & data) provided by Telecom Service Providers (TSPs). The performance of TSPs for key Quality of Service (QoS) parameters, captured during IDT are published to inform Consumers and encourage TSPs to improve their services. These IDTs have been designed to capture on ground mobile network performance of all TSPs across diverse usages environment like cities, hotspots, public transport hubs, etc.

These tests were conducted under the supervision of the TRAI Regional Office Bhopal. The observations presented in drive test reports represent the performance of the TSPs on the area/ route under test on the day/ time of conducting the drive test.

The drive tests conducted across City drive – 292.3 KMs, Hotspot locations - 7, Walk Test - 1.4 KMs, in Haridwar and Rishikesh Cities & nearby areas during 29th June 2026 to 1st July 2026 in UP West LSA.

Drive Test Route Map: The following map provides overview of drive test routes indicating City drive, Inter-operator calling, Hotspots and Walk tests, as per the legends shown on the map: -

Key Parameters Assessed

Coverage Gap: Percentage of samples, for which signal strength observed less than the minimum prescribed signal strength for respective technology (2G/ 3G/ 4G/ 5G).

Voice Services: Call Setup Success Rate (CSSR), Drop Call Rate (DCR), Call Setup Time, Call Silence (Mute) Rate, Speech Quality (MOS).

Call Silence (Mute) Instance: Number of call silence (Mute) instance occurred during the calls.

Data Servies: Download/ Upload Throughput, Latency, Jitter, Packet Drop Rate

The overall mobile network performance in Haridwar and Rishikesh city for the key parameters has been summarised below: -

a) Coverage Gap - The signal strength observed during voice testing on the drive test route in auto-selection mode (5G/4G/3G/2G), measured as the number of samples having poor signal strength out of the total samples collected, was 1534/ 50508 for Airtel, 3920/ 49983 for BSNL, 2699/ 50069 for RJIL and 952/ 50338 for VIL for Haridwar and Rishikesh City. Details of the dropped call locations have been provided in the map Annexed.

c) Call Silence Instance - Call silence instances, measured as the total number of silence instances observed for > 3 seconds out of the total calls established, were 9/ 414 for Airtel, 21/ 408 for BSNL, 18/ 435 for RJIL and 12/ 451 for VIL for Haridwar and Rishikesh City. Details of the call silence instance locations have been provided in the map Annexed.

d) Data Download and Upload Throughput:

i) Data Download performance (Overall): Average download speed was observed as 128.99 Mbps for Airtel (5G), 7.96 Mbps for BSNL (4G), 205.57 Mbps for RJIL (5G) and 58.46 Mbps for VIL (5G) for Haridwar and Rishikesh City. Detail of Download throughput has been provided in the map Annexed.

Locations of Dropped Calls and Call Silence instances can be seen by clicking red dot on the map Annexed.

Details of drive test route and area covered during the IDT is as under: -

City - The areas covered in the city drive are Doiwala, Jolly Grant, Rishikesh, Tapovan, Veerbhadra, Nepali Farm, Raiwala, Haridwar, Jwalapur, Bahadrabad, Salempur Mahdood, Devpura, Ranipur and Sitapur etc. in Haridwar & Rishikesh city.

Walk Test - The walk tests conducted on 29th June & 1st July 2026, covered Har Ki Pauri Ganga Ghat - Haridwar, Triveni Ganga Ghat – Rishikesh capturing mobile network behaviour in crowded pedestrian environments.

The findings of this IDT report have been shared with respective TSPs’ for taking further necessary action at their end. headline: Meeting of Heads of National Statistical Offices of BRICS Countries
fullText:
Ministry of Statistics & Programme Implementation

Meeting of Heads of National Statistical Offices of BRICS Countries

“Quality Statistics as Driver of Change”

03 AUG 2026 6:36PM by PIB Delhi

PRESS RELEASE- Day 1

The two-day meeting of Heads of National Statistical Offices (NSO) of BRICS Member Countries was inaugurated under the Chairship of India on 03 August 2026, at Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh, India. The event brought together more than 350 participants including representatives from National Statistical Offices of BRICS, policy makers, academia, think-tanks, civil society organisation and technical experts.

2. Guided under the overarching theme "Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability (BRICS), the BRICS Statistics track, India has adopted the theme "Quality Statistics as Driver of Change”, reflecting an unwavering commitment to data quality, innovation, effective dissemination, and people-centric statistical systems that are responsive to rapid technological advancements, the growing demand for high-frequency and granular data, and the increasing reliance on official statistics to support evidence-based, sustainable, and inclusive development.

3. The inaugural session of the Meeting of Heads of National Statistical Offices was initiated with an introduction by DG (Data Governance), MoSPI followed by an address by Shri Alok Kumar, Principal Secretary, Planning and Programme Implementation, Uttar Pradesh.

4. Dr. Saurabh Garg, Secretary, MoSPI and Chair of BRICS 2026 Statistics Track welcomed the delegates to the two-day event and highlighted key priorities of the BRICS Statistics Track 2026 centered on "Quality Statistics as a Driver of Change” including modernizing national statistical systems, utilizing administrative data and digital public infrastructure, and enhancing data governance and privacy standards. He also emphasised that, through technical exchanges and shared experiences, BRICS member nations aim to bridge data gaps, drive evidence-based decision-making, and build resilient statistical systems for the future.

5. During the inaugural session, Heads of NSOs and representatives of BRICS member countries of Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa, Egypt, Ethiopia, Indonesia, Iran and the United Arab Emirates (UAE) also shared brief introductions and their expectations from the meeting. The participating countries reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening cooperation under the BRICS Statistics Track and underscored the importance of international collaboration in advancing official statistics. They emphasised that sustained cooperation through knowledge sharing, exchange of best practices, harmonisation of statistical methodologies, and promotion of statistical innovation would enable BRICS Statistical community to strengthen the evidence base for informed policymaking, foster resilient economies, and accelerate progress towards sustainable development.

6. A draft BRICS Joint Statistical Publication (JSP), 2026 and Snapshot BRICS JSP 2026 were released on August 3, 2026 during the meeting. Any additional inputs or comments from BRICS member countries shall be incorporated subject to consensus of BRICS member countries.

7. The BRICS Main Technical Session-I, titled "From Digital Platforms to Execution-Level Experience: National Practices and Strategic Approaches for Data Dissemination," featured presentations by different member countries, namely India, Brazil, China, Egypt, Indonesia, Russia, South Africa and UAE. The presentations showcased national experiences, innovative approaches, and strategic initiatives aimed at strengthening data dissemination systems, enhancing accessibility, and promoting the effective use of official statistics in the digital era.

8. The Technical Session-II on "Transformational Reforms in Statistical System" featured presentations by India, Ethiopia, Russia, South Africa, and the United Arab Emirates (UAE), highlighting national reforms, institutional innovations, and strategies to modernise statistical systems in response to the rapidly evolving data ecosystem.

9. Besides the Technical sessions, a side-event on the theme, ‘Unlocking the potential of Administrative Data’ was also held on August 03, 2026 in collaboration with knowledge partner CivicDataLab, which was attended by representatives from BRICS member countries, civil society organizations, academia and officers from Central and State Governments. The session highlighted the growing role of administrative data as a strategic national resource for producing more timely, cost-effective, and granular official statistics, while emphasising the need for harmonised metadata, interoperable systems, and stronger institutional collaboration. The discussions concluded with a call for stronger collaboration among governments, National Statistical Offices, academia, and technology partners to build trusted data ecosystems and strengthen evidence-based policymaking.

headline: CSIR–CRRI Flags Off Indigenous Network Survey Vehicle for Urban Road Monitoring; Launches Field Survey for CAQM-Supported Standard Framework Project in Delhi NCR
fullText:
Ministry of Science & Technology

CSIR–CRRI Flags Off Indigenous Network Survey Vehicle for Urban Road Monitoring; Launches Field Survey for CAQM-Supported Standard Framework Project in Delhi NCR

03 AUG 2026 6:20PM by PIB Delhi

CSIR–Central Road Research Institute (CSIR–CRRI), New Delhi, today marked another significant milestone in advancing sustainable urban road infrastructure with the flag-off of the newly procured Indigenous Network Survey Vehicle (NSV) by Dr. Ch. Ravi Sekhar, Director, CSIR–CRRI. The event also marked the commencement of field surveys under the project titled "Implementation of the Standard Framework for Paving and Greening of Urban Roads in Delhi NCR."

The flag-off ceremony was held at the CSIR–CRRI Main Building by and attended by Dr.Ch.Ravi Sekhar, Director, CSIR-CRRI and Dr.Thallada Bhaskar, Director, CSIR-AMPRI, Bhopal and HoDs, senior scientists, officials, engineers and staff members of the Institute. The newly inducted Network Survey Vehicle will be deployed for comprehensive condition assessment of urban roads across Delhi NCR, providing scientific, accurate and data-driven inputs for road asset management and sustainable urban infrastructure planning.

Speaking on the occasion, Dr. C. Ravi Sekhar, Director, CSIR–CRRI, stated that the deployment of the indigenous Network Survey Vehicle reflects CSIR–CRRI's commitment to developing and deploying advanced technologies for smarter and more sustainable road infrastructure. He emphasized that scientific assessment of existing road conditions is essential for planning durable pavements, improving mobility, reducing maintenance costs and supporting environmentally responsible urban development.

The field survey forms an important component of the project "Implementation of the Standard Framework for Paving and Greening of Urban Roads in Delhi NCR," being implemented by CSIR–CRRI in collaboration with the Public Works Department (PWD), Government of NCT of Delhi, under a Memorandum of Agreement (MoA). The project is being undertaken in accordance with the framework of the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) for improving urban road infrastructure and mitigating dust pollution across the National Capital Region. This initiative forms part of a larger effort to implement the CAQM framework across NCR states. Under the project, CSIR-CRRI and SPA New Delhi will jointly undertake activities covering four major work packages: development of space standards and road cross-sections, mitigation of road dust through greening measures within the right-of-way, implementation of Road Asset Management Systems (RAMS) for improved maintenance practices, and promotion of innovative technologies for road construction.

The Network Survey Vehicle integrates state-of-the-art technologies, including high-speed laser profiling, UHD imaging systems, GPS/GNSS positioning, automated pavement distress mapping and AI-enabled data analytics. These capabilities enable rapid, non-contact assessment of pavement condition, road roughness, surface distress, drainage, shoulders and roadside assets while minimizing traffic disruption.

The data generated through the surveys will support scientific prioritization of maintenance works, standardized pavement design, improved drainage planning, enhanced road safety and effective monitoring of road conditions. The project is expected to contribute significantly towards reducing fugitive dust emissions, improving pavement quality and promoting sustainable urban mobility in Delhi NCR.

The event concluded with the formal flag-off of the Network Survey Vehicle and the launch of the field survey campaign, reaffirming CSIR–CRRI's leadership in providing innovative scientific solutions for national infrastructure development.

NITI Aayog in its report titled ‘Evaluation of Centrally Sponsored Schemes in Package 4 – Urban Transformation and Skill Development’ published in September 2025, has concluded that the Smart Cities Mission demonstrates strong alignment with national urban priorities and citizen needs, contributing significantly to multiple United Nations Sustainable Development Goals.
